I.     CALL TO ORDER   
 
       Mr. Bryce called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.  It should be noted 
that this meeting was held on Zoom.com with participants calling in, 
separately.   
        
II.   ROLL CALL & SEATING OF ALTERNATES 
 
       Mr. Baker called the roll and noted that there was a quorum. Mr. Bryce 
said that Ms. Tabachneck would be seated for this meeting unless other 
members of the commission arrived. He also said that the Wall St. application 
would be the last item on the agenda.

IV.   REVIEW AND ACTION ON APPLICATIONS 
        
       A. #2026-66 CSPR – Paul and Kathryn Giusti – 1 Westmere 
Avenue – demolish an existing single-family residence and construct 
a new, FEMA flood compliant single- family residence with associated 
site work adjacent to the Norwalk Harbor - Report & recommended 
action 
        
       Atty Liz Suchy began the presentation by explaining the submission of 
the application. She oriented the commissioners as to the location of the 
property on the site plan. She said that the approvals had been received from 
the required departments and the application met the regulations.  
        
       Tom Nelson, the project engineer, continued the presentation by 
explaining the existing conditions. The proposal would reduce the amount of 
impervious surfaces on the property. He showed them the proposed site plan 
with an existing sea wall. He discussed the storm water management system. 
The house will now be in compliance with flood requirements. It would also 
comply with the Connecticut Coastal Management Act.  
        
       Rob Metzgar, the architect on the project, continued the presentation 
by showing the commissioners the proposed plans. He said that there was an

unfinished lower level and the elevated first floor. He shared the exterior plans 
and noted that the proposed house is slightly larger than the current one.   
        
       There were no comments from the commissioners.  

       ** MR. JONES MOVED:  THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that 
application #2026-66 CSPR – Paul and Kathryn Giusti – 1 Westmere Avenue – 
demolish an existing single-family residence and construct a new, FEMA flood 
compliant single-family residence with associated site work adjacent to the 
Norwalk Harbor be APPROVED subject to the following conditions:

plans:

b. Per architectural plans dated 8/4/2026 prepared by Daniel Conlon 
Architects, Wilton, CT

Norwalk, CT 

d. Per planting plan dated 9/18/2026 prepared by Neil Hauck Architects, 
Darien, CT 

2. That all department sign-offs are obtained prior to issuance of any Zoning 
Permit; and 

3. That all required soil sedimentation and erosion controls are in place prior 
to the start of any construction; and 

4. That any additional needed soil sedimentation and erosion controls be 
installed at the direction of Staff; and 

5. That any changes to the plans be reviewed by Staff prior to implementation; 
and 

6. That any utilities comply with setbacks and flood regulations; and

9. All plantings be implemented prior to COZC; and

Environmental Protection and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers- obtaining such

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that these preceding conditions and 
modifications of this application are integral to the Commission’s approval 
because, if not for those conditions and modifications, the Commission would 
have denied this application. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the effective date of this approval shall be 
October 30th, 2026.

       B.     #2026-67 CSPR – 18 Marion Avenue LLC – 18 Marion 
Avenue – construct an in-ground pool, pervious patio, pool equipment, 
utility platform, outdoor shower, planters, and reconfigure front steps 
and walkway adjacent to the Norwalk Harbor - Report & recommended 
action 
        
       Robin Carrol and Arnold Carper began the presentation by explaining 
the project. It was noted that a buyer for the house wanted a pool to be 
constructed, although the house would remain the same. Ms. Carrol described 
the pool and the patio, and the outdoor shower, low planters. The remaining 
site plan had already been approved. The utility deck would be larger for the 
pool equipment.  
        
       There was a discussion as to why the pool was not part of the original 
application. There was also a discussion about pool fencing. Ms. Carrol said 
that there is an automatic cover on it so a fence is not required. The property, 
however, would be fenced. There was a discussion about the pool being close 
to the neighbors and whether they have been notified. There was also a 
discussion about whether the utility lines would be buried.  

       ** MR. JONES MOVED: THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED  that 
application #2026-67 CSPR – 18 Marion Avenue LLC – 18 Marion Avenue – 
construct an in-ground pool, pervious patio, pool equipment, utility platform, 
outdoor shower, planters, and reconfigure front steps and walkway adjacent 
to the Norwalk Harbor be APPROVED subject to the following conditions:

V. DISCUSSION 
 
       A. 535 Connecticut Avenue Pre-Application Discussion 
        
       Atty Suchy began the presentation with an introduction of the project 
team. She reminded the commissioners that they had been before them in 
May 2026. She said that they would like to adapt 535 Connecticut Avenue to  
residential units. She gave a brief description of the building and noted that 
the building was originally built for office space. She also oriented the 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 7 of 20 
 
  
         
        


commissioners as to the location of the property. She explained that some of 
the ideas that they had discussed did not seem viable at this point in time, 
including a half-office space/half residential building. She said that they would 
now discuss other ideas. One plan would include 15% affordable housing units, 
rather than the required 10%. She said that there is sufficient parking, since 
it would not be near a transportation hub.   
        
       Brooke Sugaski made comments about the office space market in 
Norwalk. She also noted that this was a Class C building. Class A buildings are 
in more desirable locations. She explained how this building could not compete 
financially to attract office tenants. She then explained the adaptive reuse into 
residential and that demolition is less desirable. They would like to help 
affordable housing by having 15% of the units be affordable. There was a 
discussion about the text amendment which would not be site specific, but 
rather, for this zone.  
        
       There was a discussion about the implication for the additional build out 
in this zone if this text amendment was to pass. Mr. Kleppin said that the staff 
had not done that. There was a discussion about SMI levels in connection with 
the affordable housing units, especially if there could be different income levels 
in the building. There was a discussion about this building being in a 
commercial zone and losing the office space. There was a discussion about the 
parking under the building and what the ratios would be. There was also a 
discussion about the density as the regulations are currently written and what 
the density would be under the proposed text change. There was a discussion 
about the size of the proposed residential units. Ms. Sugaski shared the 
proposed floor plans which included 1.5 and 2 bedroom units, as well as the 
proposed market rates for rentals of these units.  
        
       There was a discussion about recreation space and green space, both 
inside and outside the building. There will be real plantings above the parking 
deck.  There was a discussion about the valuation of the building which could 
affect the amount of taxes collected by the city. Ms. Sugaski said that the team 
could get that information. Atty Suchy noted differences between this building 
and Merritt 7, one of which was that this building was not near a transportation 
hub. Mr. Kleppin suggested contrasting this building with 200 Connecticut 
Avenue since they are in the same corridor.  
        


Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 8 of 20 
 
  
         
        


       Atty Suchy said that they would take these comments back to the team. 
Ms. Sugaski said that the building was 30% occupied when they purchased it, 
but  it is now vacant. It was too expensive to run with the low number of 
tenants so they have not made any effort to lease it. Their other option was to 
demolish the building and build retail, commercial which is permitted in this 
zone.  
        
       B. Keeler Avenue Discussion 
        
       Atty Suchy began by explaining that the Pissero family owned the 
property at 94 Keeler Avenue. She then oriented the commission as to the 
location of the property, on an aerial map. Under the revised zoning 
regulations, they could no longer subdivide the property into 4 lots, but rather, 
2 single family lots. The proposal would be to change the zone back to what it 
had been prior to the zoning updates, or to another similar zone. Atty Suchy 
said that they were before the commission for their thoughts on which zone 
change they could find appropriate, before filing an application.  
        
         There was a review of the property on the current zoning map. There 
was a discussion as to why the zone had been changed to its current one. It 
was noted that the Pissero family developed the Darinor Plaza. There was a 
review of the old zoning map in this area. There was a discussion of the B zone 
to current zones which would have similar dimensional requirements. Atty 
Suchy said that they would be back for further discussions.  
        
IV. REVIEW AND ACTION ON APPLICATIONS (con’t)  
        
       C. #2026-41 R/M/SP - Manresa Osprey LLC - Longshore Avenue 
and 0 and 3 Manresa Island (District 5, Block 86, Lots 1 and 2) - Zoning 
regulation and map amendment to create the Special District - 
Manresa Wilds (SD-MW) zoning district and special permit application 
for a Development Park Master Plan - Report & recommended action 
        
       Mr. Kleppin opened the spreadsheet that the commissioners had worked 
on at the previous meeting. There was a discussion about the number of events 
exceeding 500 people per year. There were concerns about these events and 
their effects on the neighborhood. There was also a discussion about clarifying 
the definition of events for ones that were multiple days. There was a 
discussion about having 2 events a month and keeping the minimum low. The 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 9 of 20 
 
  
         
        


applicant could submit a special permit request for more at a later date. Some 
commissioners did not think this was necessary. There was a lengthy 
discussion about the number of attendees at these events, so the 
commissioners changed the language that was confusing. They also made an 
exception for school related educational events. Mr. Bryce took a straw poll 
about some of the changes that they were discussing. There was then a 
lengthy discussion about whether the language should be limited to Norwalk 
Public Schools or to surrounding towns. The school exception was then 
removed. The commissioners said the applicant should return to the 
commission with new language for the school exception.  
        
       There was a discussion about the language for the performing arts 
center, as well as for live music. Mr. Kleppin noted that retail was added back 
in because there might be a gift shop, etc. The next document they reviewed 
was the proposed text amendment. Each phase of the project would be a new 
special permit application which would include a full traffic impact study. There 
was a discussion about receiving a draft schedule of programming to assist 
planning and traffic purposes. There was language for clarification of the 
retaining walls as well as for restaurants.  
        
       At this point, the commissioners reviewed the proposed resolution, 
focusing on the special permit conditions. There was a discussion about park 
hours which had been changed in the last few years, as well as defining 
regional parks by the city’s Recreation and Parks Department. There seemed 
to be different hours for different seasons. There were concerns about sound 
traveling over the water, later at night. There was a discussion about the hours 
of operation being later on Friday and Saturday. There was also a discussion 
about a proposed brewery not selling for off-site distribution. There was a brief 
discussion about the map. The commissioners then reviewed the Whereas 
clauses for the proposed resolutions. There would be one resolution for the 
text amendment and map change and one for the special permit. There was a 
discussion about the Whereas language in connection with the development 
park to be developed consistent with the master plan. 
        
       At this point, it was agreed that the commissioners would move to 
approve the text amendment and map change resolution first by different 
members of the commission.  


Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 10 of 20 
 
  
         
        


WHEREAS, the subject properties total approximately 125-acres located on 
Long Island Sound; 

WHEREAS, the City, in 2018, in partnership with the Manresa Association, 
conducted an economic study, including estimated remediation costs and 
potential site redevelopment scenarios; 

WHEREAS, the subject properties were previously developed and used for 
power generation; 

WHEREAS, the subject properties contain significant contamination requiring 
remediation; 

WHEREAS, the applicant is actively working with CT DEEP on remediation 
measures; 

WHEREAS, the applicant is actively working on ecological restoration; 

WHEREAS, the Commission approved application #2025 94 SP CSPR-Manresa 
Osprey, LLC, North Forest, at their February 4th 2026 meeting, which 
permitted a Park on 28.6-acres of Parcel 5-86-2, which totals approximately 
92 acres. 

WHEREAS, The North Forest provides public access and trails to property 
abutting Long Island Sound that was previously inaccessible; 

WHEREAS, the Commission, in anticipation of the submittal of applications to 
redevelop the site, at their May 20th meeting, authorized the retention of 
Creighton Manning to conduct a peer review of the traffic study and consult on 
long-term traffic planning as it relates to the redevelopment of Manresa Island; 

WHEREAS, the applicant submitted Zoning Text Amendment and Rezoning 
applications to rezone 125-acres of Manresa Island (District 5, Block 86, Lots 
1 and 2), which are currently in the CD-1S Zone, to create the Manresa Wilds 
zone; 

WHEREAS, the applicant submitted a Special Permit application to create a 
Development Park, to develop Manresa Island per a master plan to be 
approved by the Commission; 


Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 11 of 20 
 
  
         
        


WHEREAS, the Date of Receipt of the Zoning Text Amendment and Rezoning 
applications was June 3, 2026; 

WHEREAS, the Date of Receipt of the Special Permit application was June 17, 
2026; 

WHEREAS, the Commission has determined that the principal use of the site is 
a Development Park and that all other uses are accessory uses; 

WHEREAS, Creighton Manning and City staff, consulted with the applicant and 
reviewed traffic and site impacts related to the proposed development; 

WHEREAS, the Commission acknowledges that there are numerous access 
constraints to the site that warrant further study prior to the approval of any 
subsequent phases of the redevelopment; 

WHEREAS, the Commission further acknowledges that because of the unique 
nature of this site and proposed redevelopment, that tying each phase of the 
development to the conceptual master plan and requiring a separate special 
permit with accompanying traffic impact analysis will afford the City and 
neighbors the ability to fully understand impacts prior to approval and 
implementation of each phase; 

WHEREAS, the Commission has determined that the Visitation and Visitor 
Projections, prepared by ORCA Consulting, LLC and Transportation Strategy 
Memorandum prepared by AKRF are appropriate levels of traffic analysis to 
approve the Zoning Text Amendment and Rezoning; 

WHEREAS, the Commission has determined that the Visitation and Visitor 
Projections, prepared by ORCA Consulting, LLC and Transportation Strategy 
Memorandum prepared by AKRF are appropriate levels of traffic analysis to 
approve the Special Permit application, which approves the use of the site as 
a Development Park, to be developed consistent with the conceptual master 
plan; 

WHEREAS, the Commission has determined that based on expert testimony 
provided by City Transportation Mobility and Parking (TMP) Staff, AKRF and 
Creighton Manning, that full Traffic Impact Studies are necessary for each 
subsequent phase of the project and is in agreement regarding the scope of 
the analysis agreed to by TMP, Creighton Manning and AKRF; 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 12 of 20 
 
  
         
        


WHEREAS, the Commission acknowledges that based on testimony and 
analysis conducted to date that there are numerous access constraints to the 
site that warrant further study prior to the approval of any subsequent phases 
of the redevelopment; 

WHEREAS, in a letter to the Commission dated August 5, 2026, CT DEEP stated 
that “at a conceptual level, we find the upland aspects of the Master Plan, 
which align with what has been discussed in pre-application meetings with 
DEEP, consistent with the CCMA, noting that detailed site plans for the 
development, which the development timeline shows are expected to follow in 
2027, will be subjected to a more in-depth review. These site plans are 
expected to be proposed in accordance with guidance provided in continuing 
regular meetings with DEEP staff, including our Land and Water Resources, 
Remediation, Wildlife, Fisheries, and Boating sections, to ensure consistency 
with all applicable regulations”; 

WHEREAS, at their regularly scheduled meeting held July 22, 2026 the Harbor 
Management Commission determined that the proposal to create the Manresa 
Wilds (SD-MW) zoning district and special permit application for a 
Development Park Master Plan is consistent with the Harbor Management Plan; 

WHEREAS, redevelopment and reuse of the site prioritizing public access to 
the trails, grounds and site amenities, as well as access to Long Island Sound, 
is beneficial to the City; 

WHEREAS, the Commission conducted a public hearing on the proposed 
applications at a special meeting on June 24, 2026, at which time written and 
verbal testimony was received; 

WHEREAS, the Commission continued the public hearing on the proposed 
applications at their regular meeting on July 15, 2026, at which time written 
and verbal testimony was received; 

WHEREAS, the Commission continued the public hearing on the proposed 
applications at a special meeting on July 29, 2026, at which time additional 
written and verbal testimony was received; 

WHEREAS, the Commission continued the public hearing on the proposed 
applications at their regular meeting on August 19, 2026, at which time 
additional written and verbal testimony was received; 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 13 of 20 
 
  
         
        


WHEREAS, the Commission continued the public hearing on the proposed 
applications at their regular meeting on September 2, 2026, at which time 
additional written and verbal testimony was received; 

WHEREAS, the Commission continued the public hearing on the proposed 
applications at a special meeting on September 24, 2026, at which time 
additional written and verbal testimony was received; 

WHEREAS, the Commission considered all testimony received and closed the 
hearing on the three applications on September 24, 2026; 

WHEREAS, the Commission conducted deliberations on the three applications 
at a special meeting on October 14, 2026; 

WHEREAS, the Commission concluded deliberations on the three applications 
at their regular meeting on October 21, 2026 and made the following additional 
findings: 

WHEREAS, the Commission finds the application meets the standards for 
Special Permit as indicated in Article 8.4.8 of the Zoning Regulations since this 
application is for a Development Park, that must be developed consistent with 
the conceptual plan; and 

WHEREAS, the Commission recognizes site programming will change over time 
and that activities, events (including the number and size) and uses will 
change, requiring future modifications to this approval; 

       ** MR. JONES MOVED: THEREFORE BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED, 
by the Norwalk Planning & Zoning Commission that Zoning Text Amendment 
and Rezoning applications to rezone 125-acres of Manresa Island proposed as 
part of application #2026-41 R/M/SP - Manresa Osprey LLC - Longshore 
Avenue and 0 and 3 Manresa Island (District 5, Block 86, Lots 1 and 2) - Zoning 
regulation and map amendment to create the Special District - Manresa Wilds 
(SD-MW) zoning district and special permit application for a Development Park 
Master Plan, be  APPROVED  to implement the following goals, policies, 
strategies and actions of the Norwalk Plan of Conservation and Development: 

Chapter 7: Goal 1, Strategy b.ii 

Pursue planning and funding for public access to Long Island Sound on Manresa 
Island, for example, remediation that allows for a coastal walking trail. Work 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 14 of 20 
 
  
         
        


with the owners, environmental organizations, and other stakeholders to 
preserve the maximum area possible on Manresa Island as natural open space 
with some public access and maintain a water dependent use. 

Chapter 7: Goal 1, Strategy c.ii 

Continue working with the Manresa Association to establish open space on the 
Manresa peninsula and maintain a water dependent use. 

Chapter 9: Goal 2, Strategy a.i 

Advocate to preserve the northern section of Manresa Island (92 acres) as a 
conservation area. Plan for the rest of the site to have uses that are consistent 
with the Harbor Management Plan principles 

Chapter 9: Goal 4, Strategy a.iii 

Seek public access to the coast in disposition plans for Manresa Island. 

Chapter 12: Goal 3 

“The user-friendly zoning ordinance is consistent with the future land use map 
and achievement of the vision and goals of the POCD.” 

a. Policy: “Support revision of the zoning ordinance to promote desired 
development and design patterns.” 

b. Policy: “Support permit streamlining for projects with desired 
characteristics.” 

i. Strategy A: Action i: “Rewrite the zoning ordinance to reflect contemporary 
best practices in administration and user-friendliness and to be consistent with 
the POCD.” 

       Ms. Langalis seconded.  
        
        
       Mr. Kleppin said that the Connecticut Department of Energy and 
Environmental Protection (DEEP) found it is consistent with the regulations as 
well as the Harbor Management Commission with the Harbor Management 
Plan.

as part of application #2026-41 R/M/SP - Manresa Osprey LLC - Longshore 
Avenue and 0 and 3 Manresa Island (District 5, Block 86, Lots 1 and 2) - 
Zoning regulation and map amendment to create the Special District - 
Manresa Wilds (SD-MW) zoning district and special permit application for a 
Development Park Master Plan, be APPROVED subject to the following 
conditions: 

1. All conditions of approval for Planning and Zoning Commission application 
#2025-94 SP CSPR, Manresa Osprey are still applicable. 

2. The 28.6-acre North Forest, which was approved as application #2025 94 
SP CSPR-Manresa Osprey, LLC, North Forest, be placed under a conservation 
easement, with appropriate allowances for the applicant to operate the site in 
accordance with its approvals, including infrastructure improvements. 

3. The easement become part of the Master Plan and that the easement be 
placed on the land records prior to commencement of any site activity 
conducted as part of any subsequent phases of the project. 

4. All future redevelopment of the site be consisted with the conceptual 
master plan dated May, 2026, unless further modified and approved by the 
Commission; 

5. Public parking capacity be limited to 200 vehicles as proposed by the 
applicant until such time that the applicant can demonstrate to the 
satisfaction of the Commission that additional capacity is needed. 

6. Any parking structure proposed in the future shall be subject to design 
approval and approval of screening by the Commission. 

7. Data Centers are prohibited, including but not limited to those defined in 
Conn. Gen. Stat. Section 32-286. 

Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 16 of 20 
 
  
         
        


8. Park hours shall be consistent with Norwalk Regional Park hours, as 
indicated by the Recreation and Parks Department. 

9. Unless otherwise noted in the approval, all scheduled programming, 
excluding events, shall cease at park close. 

10. For purposes of this approval, events shall be: 

a. considered activities that are singular and not part of scheduled 
programming; or 

b. part of occurring within space offered to outside non-profit or community 
organizations. 

11. Events within either designated Event Space, Auditorium, Performing Arts 
Centers or elsewhere on the grounds are subject to the following: USE 
SPREADSHEET LANGUAGE 

a. There shall be no more than 4 events per month with attendance 
exceeding 150 guests. 

b. There shall be no more than 4 Events per year (excluding any grand 
opening events) exceeding 500 people. 

c. Except for School-related events, events exceeding 150 people requires a 
special events permit per City Code Ch 88. 

d. Maximum event capacity cannot exceed 800 people. 

e. Should there be an event occurring in an event space and a second 
event(s) occurring simultaneously within the theater, auditorium, performing 
arts center or another event space, maximum capacity shall not exceed 
1,000 people. 

12. Brew Pub/Distilleries are permitted, provided that: 

a. They shall not exceed 7,500 sf 

b. No on-site packaging for off-site distribution or sales. 

13. Restaurants are permitted, provided that they shall not exceed 7,500 sf 


Planning & Zoning Commission - Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
Page 17 of 20 
 
  
         
        


14. Maximum theater capacity is 300 seats. 

15. Outdoor amphitheaters can only be located as depicted on the approved 
master plan, unless the master plan is modified and approved by the 
Commission. 

16. Outdoor amphitheaters are limited to 100 people, unless a Special Permit 
is granted. 

17. Any Boat Terminal is subject to a Harbor Safety Plan to be reviewed and 
approved by the Harbor Master and Harbor Management Commission. 

18. Live Music shall comply with Chapter 68 (Noise) of the Town Code. 

19. Unless explicitly indicated in these regulations, site development shall 
conform to all other applicable criteria in the regulations. 

20. A Special Permit certificate shall be filed on the Norwalk Land Records. 

RESOLVED, THAT, that the effective date of this action shall be November 
16, 2026. 

       Ms. Langalis seconded.  
       Chapin Bryce; Tammy Langalis; Diana Lenkowsky; Louis

       Jones; Jackie Jordan-Byron approved.  
       No one opposed.  
       No one abstained. 
        
       Mr. Bryce thanked the commissioners and the applicant for the time

thoughtful commentary. She said the applicant looked forward to moving 
forward with the project. Mr. Bryce also thanked the public for the comments.

       Mr. Kleppin said that the commissioners are required to do some training 
hours for certification but a couple of commissioners are not compliant. He said 
that if anyone wants to attend a program in mid-November, he would forward 
the information. He would also confirm how long the certification was good for.

he would let them know. There would be one meeting in December.
